newGuidanceLeaves.text: UA p. 18 distinguishes the initial specialization choice, made when the character is created, from double specialization, which a fighter or ranger may choose initially or later for the same specific weapon type already specialized in. Double specialization is limited to melee weapons other than pole arms and the two-handed sword; it uses the proficiency slot that would otherwise gain a new weapon and grants +3 to hit and +3 damage. For ordinary melee specialization, +1 to hit and +2 damage stack with Strength and magic bonuses, and the weapon must be a specific type (for example, long sword rather than “sword”). For a crossbow specialist, the 6–60-foot point-blank category completely replaces a light crossbow’s ordinary short range in a dungeon.
UA p. 21 distinguishes the outdoor base-chance ceiling of 110% from the final adjusted chance: after modifiers, an adjusted chance above 100% is treated as 100%.

UA p. 18 distinguishes the initial specialization choice, made when the character is created, from double specialization, which a fighter or ranger may choose initially or later for the same specific weapon type already specialized in. Double specialization is limited to melee weapons other than pole arms and the two-handed sword; it uses the proficiency slot that would otherwise gain a new weapon and grants +3 to hit and +3 damage. For ordinary melee specialization, +1 to hit and +2 damage stack with Strength and magic bonuses, and the weapon must be a specific type (for example, long sword rather than “sword”). For a crossbow specialist, the 6–60-foot point-blank category completely replaces a light crossbow’s ordinary short range in a dungeon.

UA p. 20 names eight locale- or culture-selected tertiary skill options: animal handling, horsemanship, long-distance signalling, running, small craft (paddled), small craft (rowed), sound imitation, and snare building. The DM determines which apply to the campaign; a barbarian has one or more.
